transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

I guess… work, mostly. I mean, I’ve always had stressful days, but this has felt different. We got a new operations manager, and ever since he started going over the inspection procedures I’ve used for years and picking them apart like I suddenly don’t know how to do my job, I just can’t seem to shut it off when I leave.

I’ll come home still wound up from meetings, replaying every little comment in my head, and then I’m short with my husband over things that really don’t deserve that kind of reaction. Then I’m lying awake at night going back through what was said, what I should’ve said, whether I missed something. And the next day at work, I’m second-guessing quality calls that used to be routine for me—things I would’ve made without blinking before. It’s just gotten to where I don’t feel like myself.
Can you tell me if you've been feeling down or hopeless about things, or if your main struggle has been more about feeling anxious or on edge?

It’s more like I’m anxious and on edge, I think. I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling hopeless exactly. It’s just that ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I can’t seem to leave work at work anymore.

I come home wound up, like I’m still in those meetings, and then I’ll snap at my husband over something small because I’m already so tense. And at night I’m lying there replaying what was said, what he questioned, whether I handled it right. Then the next day I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble. So… yes, more anxious, more keyed up, like I can’t settle.
Do you find yourself having the same worrisome thoughts over and over, even when you're trying not to think about them?

Yes… definitely. It’s like the same loop keeps starting over in my head, even when I’m trying to do something else. I’ll be home, and I know I’m not at work anymore, but I’m still thinking about what the new operations manager said, how he questioned the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, whether I explained myself clearly enough, whether I missed something obvious.

And I’ll tell myself, “Just let it go, you’ve done this job a long time,” but then five minutes later I’m replaying the same meeting again. It carries into the evening, and I’m wound up enough that I’ll snap at my husband over something small, and then I feel bad about that too. Then at night it’s worse because there’s nothing distracting me, so I’m lying there going over every comment and every quality call in my head. By the next day, even routine decisions I used to make without a second thought feel like something I have to second-guess.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms along with all of this, like feeling restless, tense muscles, or being easily fatigued?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I know I feel wound up, but I don’t know if I’ve paid enough attention to my body to say it’s tense muscles or fatigue in a clear way. I haven’t been sitting there thinking, “Oh, my shoulders hurt because of this,” if that makes sense.

It’s more that I notice my mind won’t settle, and then I suppose my body feels… keyed up along with it, but I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t noticed anything really specific or dramatic physically. I think I’ve been so focused on what’s happening at work and replaying all of that that I may not be separating out what’s mental from what’s physical very well.

Have you ever had a sudden episode where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came on quickly and peaked within minutes, maybe including symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you couldn’t breathe?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, where it suddenly comes on really hard and peaks in a few minutes. I mean, I get worked up, and I can feel very keyed up about the work situation, but it’s more like it builds and stays with me, if that makes sense.

I haven’t had an episode where I thought, “Oh my gosh, I can’t breathe,” or where I suddenly started sweating or trembling out of nowhere. At least, not that I’ve noticed. It’s more of a constant tension in my head, like I’m stuck on the same worry, rather than a sharp attack that comes and goes quickly.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain situations, tasks, or people at work because of the stress or worry about how they might go?

Yes… I have. I don’t like admitting that, because I’ve always been someone who just shows up and does what’s expected, but lately I’ve been pulling back.

Meetings are the biggest thing. If I know the new operations manager is going to be there, or if there’s a chance my inspection procedures are going to be questioned again, I’ll find myself trying to avoid being in the room unless I absolutely have to. Sometimes I’ll tell myself I’m too busy with the actual inspection work, or I’ll delay responding, but honestly part of it is that I’m worried about how it’s going to go and whether I’m going to get put on the spot.

And it’s starting to show in my work record, which really bothers me. I’ve missed some internal deadlines because I keep second-guessing things or putting off the parts where I might have to explain or defend my decisions. That’s not like me. I’ve always been dependable, and now I feel like I’m creating more problems by trying to avoid the stressful parts.

At home it’s been spilling over too. My husband and I are arguing more, usually over things that probably wouldn’t have turned into arguments before. And I’m not keeping up with our normal evening routines the way I used to — just the regular things we’d do after work. I either don’t have the focus for it or I’m still stuck thinking about what happened at work, so things just… don’t get done the same way.
Has the stress and worry you’re feeling been limited mostly to your job situation, or have you noticed similar anxiety in other parts of your life as well?

It started with work, very clearly. I don’t think I was like this before the new operations manager came in and started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. That’s the thing I keep coming back to, because I’ve done this job a long time and I used to trust my judgment. I’d make routine quality calls and move on with my day.

Now it’s like I can’t leave it there. I come home still wound up, still thinking through what was said in a meeting or what might be questioned next. And then it spills into home because I’m tense and distracted, and I end up snapping at my husband over things that probably aren’t really about him. I’ll lie awake replaying conversations from work, thinking about whether I said the wrong thing or whether one of my decisions is going to get challenged.

So I wouldn’t say I’m anxious about everything in life in the same way. It’s mostly tied to the job situation. But it doesn’t stay neatly at work anymore, if that makes sense. It follows me home, and then it affects how I am at home too.
Have you ever felt anxious or worried when you're away from home or separated from your husband, even outside of work stress?

I don’t think so, no. Not really in that way.

I mean, I’m used to being on my own during the day, and I don’t feel like I can’t manage if I’m not at home or if my husband isn’t right there. If I’m away from him, I don’t usually get anxious just because of that. It’s more that if I’m already wound up from work, then I might want to talk to him or I might be more irritable when I do see him, but I wouldn’t say I’m afraid to be separated from him or worried something will happen because we’re apart.

And being away from home by itself isn’t usually the issue either. If I’m out running errands or doing normal things, I don’t notice that same kind of worry unless my mind drifts back to work. So… no, I don’t think it’s about being away from home or away from my husband. It’s more connected to what’s been happening at work.
Outside of the stress you’re feeling about work, have you noticed yourself feeling anxious or worried when you’re away from home or separated from your husband, even during normal daily routines?

No, I really haven’t noticed that outside of the work stress. I mean, I can go run errands, go to appointments, be out doing normal daily things, and I’m not sitting there worrying because I’m away from home or because my husband isn’t with me.

If I feel anxious during the day, it’s usually because my mind has drifted back to something at work — like replaying a conversation or thinking about what might happen next — not because I’m separated from him. I don’t feel like I need him right there to feel safe or okay. It’s more that when I’m already stressed, I might want to talk to him about it later, or I might be tense when I get home.

So… no, I don’t think that’s really been a thing for me. It’s not the being away from home or him. It’s where my head goes about work.
Have you ever found yourself feeling anxious or worried about things unrelated to work, like everyday decisions or responsibilities, even when there's no immediate stressor?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I do have normal worries like anybody does — if there’s a bill to pay or something around the house that needs deciding, I can think about it — but it doesn’t usually take over on its own when there isn’t some reason for it.

Lately, when I catch myself feeling really wound up or second-guessing things, it almost always has a thread back to work somehow. Like I might be making dinner or trying to decide what needs doing at home, and then suddenly I’m thinking about something someone said at work, or whether I handled something the right way. So it can look like I’m anxious during everyday things, but in my mind it’s not really about the everyday thing.

I don’t generally sit around worrying about random responsibilities for no reason, or feeling anxious about ordinary decisions if nothing else is going on. It’s more like the work stress keeps following me into those moments.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or worried about things that aren't related to work, even when there's nothing specific happening that would usually cause you to worry?

Not really in a separate way, no. I mean, I do feel anxious, but when I actually trace it back, it’s almost always tied to what’s been going on at work.

Ever since this new operations manager started, he’s been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, and it’s like I can’t shut it off anymore. I’ll come home already wound up, and then I’m replaying meetings in my head or thinking about something he questioned, and then I’ll snap at my husband over something small. Or I’ll be trying to relax and my mind goes right back to, “Did I explain that right?” or “Is he going to challenge that decision tomorrow?”

So it’s not like I’m just sitting around worrying out of nowhere about random things. It feels like work follows me home, and then even routine things I used to do without thinking — quality calls I’ve made for years — I start second-guessing the next day. That’s the part that feels new and upsetting.

Have you noticed yourself feeling anxious or worried about being judged or criticized in situations outside of work, like during social interactions or when making everyday decisions in front of others?

I don’t think so, not outside of work. I mean, I can be self-conscious like anyone, especially if I’m tired or already upset, but I haven’t really noticed myself worrying that friends or people at the grocery store or wherever are judging me.

If I’m making an everyday decision in front of someone — like choosing something at a store, or talking with a neighbor, or ordering food — I’m not sitting there thinking, “Oh no, they’re going to criticize me.” That’s not really where my mind goes.

The judged-or-criticized feeling is much more tied to work, because that’s where I feel like what I’m doing is being questioned. Outside of that, I might still be a little tense because I’m carrying it around with me, but it’s not like I’m afraid people socially are evaluating me. It’s really more specific than that.
Have you ever felt anxious or worried about being evaluated or performing poorly in situations outside of work, like when you're doing something in front of others or trying something new?

I don’t think that’s really been a thing for me outside of work, no. I mean, if I’m trying something new, sure, I might feel a little awkward at first — like anyone would, I think — but I don’t usually get caught up worrying that I’m going to perform badly or that people are watching me and judging how I’m doing.

Like, if I’m doing something in front of other people in a normal setting, I might want to do it right, but I’m not sitting there with that same tight feeling of being evaluated. That feeling is much more connected to work for me, where my decisions or the way I do things feel like they’re under a microscope.

Outside of that, I haven’t noticed myself avoiding things or getting especially anxious just because someone might see me make a mistake. It’s not really something I think about much unless work is already on my mind.

Have you ever felt anxious or worried when there wasn’t anything specific going on—like when things were actually calm—or does the anxiety always seem to have a clear cause like a work-related stressor?

It pretty much has a clear cause, as far as I can tell. I don’t usually get anxious when everything is genuinely calm and nothing is happening. It’s more like… work has stopped being contained to work, if that makes sense.

Ever since the new operations manager came in and started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I feel like I can’t just leave it there at the end of the day. I come home already wound up, and then I’m still carrying the whole thing with me. I’ll replay a meeting in my head, or go over something he questioned, or wonder if I should have explained a quality call differently.

And then even at home, when there isn’t anything actually happening right that second, I’m not calm because my mind is still back at work. I’ll snap at my husband over something that really isn’t the issue, and later I know it wasn’t about him. Or I’ll lie awake thinking through conversations from earlier in the day. Then the next day I find myself second-guessing routine inspection decisions I used to make without much trouble.

So it can look like it’s coming up during a quiet moment, but to me it doesn’t feel random. It feels like the work stress is following me into the quiet moments.
Have you ever felt anxious or worried even when there wasn’t anything specific to be stressed about, like on days when everything at work went smoothly or there were no problems at home?

Not really in the way you’re asking, I don’t think. Even on days when nothing obvious is happening right in that moment, it usually still feels connected to work.

I’m here because ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I just can’t seem to leave work at work anymore. So even if a day goes mostly smoothly, or there aren’t problems at home, I’ll still come home wound up because I’m thinking about what was questioned, or whether I handled something right, or whether I’m going to get criticized for a quality call that used to feel routine to me.

It’s not like I’m sitting there calm and then anxiety appears out of nowhere. It’s more like the work stress stays in my system. I’ll replay meetings in my head, and then I’m short with my husband over something small, and later I realize I was still carrying that tension. Or I’ll go to bed and my mind goes right back to work, even if nothing is actually happening at home.

So I guess if everything at work truly went smoothly and I wasn’t thinking about it, I wouldn’t expect to feel that anxious. But lately, even “smooth” days don’t always feel smooth, because I’m second-guessing routine decisions I used to make without trouble.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or worried in social situations or while performing everyday tasks in front of others, even when work isn’t on your mind?

No, I can’t really say I’ve noticed that. I mean, I’m not someone who loves being the center of attention or anything, but everyday things like talking to people, being in a store, doing something while someone else is nearby — that doesn’t usually make me anxious on its own.

If work isn’t in my head, I don’t find myself worrying much about people watching me or judging me. I might have a normal moment of feeling self-conscious, like if I’m doing something clumsy or I don’t know how something works, but it passes. It’s not the kind of worry that sticks with me or makes me avoid doing things.

So I’d say no, not really. The anxious feeling I’ve been talking about seems much more tied to the work situation than to social situations in general.
